## Description

The Python 3 program reads two positive integers \(N\) and \(M\) from standard input. It prints the sum of the powers of \(N\) from exponent \(0\) through \(M\) when the sum is at most \(10^9\), and prints `inf` otherwise.

## Preconditions

- PRE-1 (Unverified) — Standard input contains two integers on one line, with \(N\) first and \(M\) second.
- PRE-2 (Unverified) — \(1 \le N \le 10^9\).
- PRE-3 (Unverified) — \(1 \le M \le 100\).

## Postconditions

- POST-1 (Unverified) — \(X\) is the exact integer sum \(\sum_{i=0}^{M}N^i\). Both endpoint terms are included, and each exponent contributes once, even when several terms have the same value. In particular, \(X=M+1\) when \(N=1\).
- POST-2 (Unverified) — If \(X\le 10^9\), stdout contains one line with the decimal integer \(X\). This includes the equality case, which prints `1000000000`.
- POST-3 (Unverified) — If \(X>10^9\), stdout contains one line with exactly the lowercase text `inf`.

## Test suggestions

Each stdin and stdout entry is a single line.

| Stdin | Expected stdout | Conditions and coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `1 100` | `101` | PRE-2, PRE-3, POST-1, POST-2. Minimum base and maximum exponent, with every term equal to one. |
| `2 1` | `3` | PRE-3, POST-1, POST-2. Minimum exponent, with both endpoint terms required. |
| `10 8` | `111111111` | POST-1, POST-2. Every power through the eighth contributes a digit. |
| `10 9` | `inf` | POST-1, POST-3. The highest power equals the threshold and the full sum exceeds it. |
| `1000000000 1` | `inf` | PRE-2, PRE-3, POST-1, POST-3. Maximum base, with the sum one above the threshold. |

## Unspecified behavior

The statement gives no required behavior for missing or extra input values, non-integer values, or integers outside the stated ranges.
